body: A deep clean is for the house that needs more than upkeep: the first clean with a new cleaner, a seasonal reset, getting ready to host, or catching up after a busy few months. In Atlanta homes that usually means pollen film on sills and fans, red clay ground into entry floors, and soap scum and mildew in bathrooms that run humid most of the year.

Sweet Tea Cleaning Co. works top to bottom, room by room. We start high with fans, vents and light fixtures, work down through cabinet fronts, baseboards and door frames, and finish with floors so nothing falls onto a surface that is already clean. Bathrooms get scrubbed tile and grout and descaled glass. Kitchens get degreased fronts and the inside of the oven and fridge.

Deep cleans take longer than regular visits, so we confirm the size and condition of the home up front and give you a clear quote before we start. Many clients follow a deep clean with recurring service, because the hard part is already done.

body: Renovation dust is different from everyday dust. It is fine enough to sit on top of cabinets, inside drawers, along every ledge and in the air for days, and a normal clean just moves it around. In Metro Atlanta, where a lot of older homes are being opened up and updated, post-construction cleaning is the step that turns a job site back into a home.

Sweet Tea Cleaning Co. cleans from the top down: light fixtures, fans and vents first, then cabinets inside and out, counters, windows, sills and tracks, and finally floors. We remove paint flecks, sticker residue and adhesive from new fixtures and glass, and vacuum and damp-wipe so fine dust is picked up instead of pushed around.

Most projects need the clean after the trades finish and before furniture moves in. Some benefit from a rough clean followed by a final touch-up. Send us photos or a description of the job and your move-in date, and we will quote the scope that fits.

about_paragraphs: In-town Atlanta is a patchwork of housing. Midtown and Buckhead are stacked with high-rise condos and apartments, Virginia-Highland and Inman Park are full of 1910s-1930s bungalows and Victorians, and Old Fourth Ward and West Midtown keep adding lofts and townhomes along the BeltLine. A lot of those units turn over as short-term rentals, and nearly every one of them sits under the tree canopy that gives Atlanta its name.

That canopy is beautiful until March. Pine and oak pollen coats balconies, window sills, ceiling fans and anything near a patio door, and it comes back inside on every pair of shoes. In the high-rises, the challenge is access instead: concierge check-in, elevator bookings and garage rules decide when a cleaner can get in and how long they can stay.

We plan for both. In pollen season we hand-wipe sills, tracks, fan blades and screens instead of just dusting them, which only spreads the film around. In condo buildings we check in with the concierge, follow loading and parking rules and bring compact equipment, and for BeltLine rentals we schedule turnovers straight from your booking calendar.

areas.location_note: No extra travel fee in this area
areas.about_heading: Gentle, Detailed Cleaning for Decatur's Older Homes
about_paragraphs: Decatur sits about six miles east of downtown Atlanta and serves as the county seat of DeKalb County. Around the courthouse square, neighborhoods like Oakhurst, Winnona Park and Midway Woods are lined with bungalows and craftsman homes from the 1920s to the 1950s, many lovingly renovated, many still wearing their original oak floors, hex tile bathrooms and plaster walls. It is also our home base.

Older homes show dirt differently. Hardwood finishes worn thin by decades of use dull quickly with harsh cleaners, vintage grout stains easily, and the deep trim, tall baseboards and window sills of a craftsman home catch dust and pollen that newer, flatter surfaces shed. Bathrooms with original fixtures and limited ventilation stay damp through the summer, so mildew finds caulk and grout lines fast.

We clean these homes with a slower hand. We use pH-neutral products on old wood and tile, hand-detail trim, sills and baseboards instead of skimming over them, and scrub grout and caulk lines in older bathrooms so they dry clean. Many Decatur clients start with a deep clean and then keep the house there with recurring visits.
